Ladies and gentlemen, THIS IS THE COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA. This is embarrassing. Absolutely embarrassing. President Donald Trump was asked about Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, a male U.S. Army officer who previously commanded the 101st Airborne Division. Trump repeatedly referred to him as “she,” while confidently discussing the serious consequences this officer supposedly faces. The President of the United States is publicly discussing a senior military officer, threatening long-term consequences, and doesn’t even appear to know who he’s talking about. And some of you defend this man no matter what. Now, here’s where things get predictable. I’m going to post this video, and instead of addressing what’s directly in front of you, I already expect the usual responses. Here comes a meme about Democrats. Here comes something about transgender people. Here comes an insult about liberals, Biden, Obama, or anybody else you want to drag into the conversation. Anything except addressing the actual video. And that’s precisely my point. I’m not personally attacking YOU. I’m criticizing the performance of the person you voted for and continue defending. There’s a difference. But some of you have become so personally invested in defending Donald Trump that you treat every criticism of him as an attack on your own identity. That’s where cognitive dissonance enters the conversation. When the evidence conflicts with what you desperately want to believe, some of you change the subject instead of confronting the evidence. And the funniest part? Nobody is forcing you to respond. You have every right to scroll past this video. But some of you won’t. You’ll feel compelled to defend him, even when your response has absolutely nothing to do with what happened. A transgender meme doesn’t explain this video. An insult about Democrats doesn’t explain this video. A picture of Joe Biden doesn’t explain this video. And attacking me personally doesn’t change a single word coming out of Donald Trump’s mouth. The video speaks for itself. This is the commander-in-chief. The person responsible for leading the United States Armed Forces. The person making decisions involving national security, military operations, and the lives of American service members. And here’s the part I find particularly troubling: He’s speaking confidently about potential consequences for a senior military officer while apparently not even recognizing who the officer is. We’re talking about Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, not some obscure individual with no connection to military leadership. You don’t have to be a Democrat to recognize why this deserves scrutiny. You don’t have to be a liberal to expect the president to know the senior military officials he’s publicly discussing. And you certainly don’t have to defend every mistake a politician makes simply because you voted for him. With the midterms approaching, Americans have every reason to examine the conduct and accountability of the people holding power. If you disagree with my assessment, address the video. Explain why you believe this performance is acceptable from the commander-in-chief. But if your entire response consists of some unrelated meme, personal insult, or attack on Democrats, you’re demonstrating the exact behavior I’m describing. At some point, defending the indefensible becomes more embarrassing than the original incident. Watch the video. Listen to his words. And ask yourself one simple question: If this were any other president, would you be making the same excuses?
